interaction.def: Two objects acting on each other: pushing, pulling, rubbing or attracting. Every force is one side of an interaction.

force.def: A push or pull exerted on an object by another object, with a size and a direction (a vector). Unit: the newton, 1 N = 1 kg·m/s².

contact-force.def: A force between objects that touch: the normal force, tension and friction. At the scale of atoms these are electric forces between the surfaces.

long-range-force.def: A force between objects that do not touch. In this course the only one is gravity, such as Earth's pull on a falling ball.

agent-of-force.def: The object that exerts a force. A free-body diagram label names the type and the agent: "F_N, floor on box".

free-body-diagram.def: A diagram of one object (a dot at its center of mass) with every force exerted on it by other objects drawn as a whole arrow starting on the dot, labeled with its type and agent, lengths in proportion. It never shows velocity, components or a net force arrow.

normal-force.def: The push of a surface on an object touching it, perpendicular to the surface and away from it (F_N). Its size is whatever the situation requires, not always mg.

tension.def: The pull of a rope, string or cable on an object attached to it, directed along the rope away from the object (F_T).

weight.def: The pull of Earth (or another planet) on an object, F_g = mg, pointing down toward the planet's center. Near Earth, g = 9.8 m/s² (10 m/s² is accepted). Mass stays the same everywhere; weight depends on where you are.

net-force.def: The vector sum of all the forces on an object, ΣF. It is found from the free-body diagram and is not itself one of the forces.
